source_text: Haec ita dispecta totum ordinem dei iudicis operarium et, ut dignius dixerim, protectorem catholicae et summae illius bonitatis ostendunt, quam (ut) semotam a iudiciariis sensibus et in suo statu puram nolunt Marcionitae in eodem deo agnoscere, pluente super bonos et malos et solem suum oriri faciente super iustos et iniustos, quod alius deus omnino non praestat. nam etsi hoc quoque testimonium Christi in creatorem Marcion. de euangelio eradere ausus est, sed ipse mundus inscriptus est et omni a conscientia legitur. et erit haec ipsa patientia creatoris in iudicium Marcionis, illa patientia, quae expectat paenitentiam potius peccatoris quam mortem et mauult misericordiam quam sacrificium, auertens destinatum iam exitium Niniuitis et largiens spatium uitae Ezechiae lacrimis et restituens statum regni Babylonis tyranno paenitentia functo: illam dico misericordiam, quae et filium Saulis moriturum ex deuotione populo concessit et Dauid delicta in domum Uriae confessum uenia liberauit et ipsum Israhel totiens restituit quotiens iudicauit, totiens refouit quotiens et increpuit. non solum igitur iudicem aspiciens conuertere et ad optimi exempla: notans cum ulciscitur considera cum indulget; repende austeritati lenitatem. cum utrumque conueneris in creatore, inuenies in eo et illud, propter quod alterum deum credis. ueni denique ad inspectationem doctrinarum disciplinarum praeceptorum consiliorumque eius. dices forsitan haec etiam humanis legibus determinari. sed ante Lycurgos et Solonas omnes Moyses et deus. nulla posteritas non a primordiis accipit. tamen non a tuo deo didicit creator meus praescribere : non occides, non adulterabis, non furaberis, non falsum testimonium dices, alienum non concupisces, honora patrem et matrem, et diliges proximum tuum ut temetipsum. ad haec innocentiae et pudicitiae, iustitiae et pietatis principalia consulta accedunt etiam humanitatis praescripta, cum septimo quoque anno seruitia libertate soluuntur, cum eodem tempore agro parcitur egenis cedendo locum, (cum) boui etiam terenti uincula oris remittuntur ad fructum praesentis laboris, quo facilius in pecudibus praemeditata humanitas in hominum refrigeria erudiretur.
pass_a_gloss: These things, having been thus considered, show the entire order of God the judge and, that I may say it more worthily, the protector of the catholic and highest goodness, which the Marcionites do not want to recognize in the same God, who rains upon the good and the evil and makes his sun rise upon the just and the unjust, which another God altogether does not provide. For even if Marcion has dared to erase this testimony of Christ from the creator from the gospel, the world itself is inscribed and is read by every conscience. And this patience of the creator will be in judgment against Marcion, that patience which waits for the repentance of the sinner rather than death and prefers mercy to sacrifice, turning away the destined destruction of Nineveh and granting a space of life to Hezekiah with tears and restoring the state of the kingdom of Babylon to the tyrant who has done penance: I say that mercy, which also granted the son of Saul who was to die from devotion to the people and freed David from guilt, confessed in the house of Uriah, with free pardon and restored Israel as many times as it judged, as many times as it rebuked. Not only, therefore, looking at the judge, does one turn and convert to the best examples: noting when he takes revenge, considering when he indulges; weighing leniency against austerity. When you have considered both in the creator, you will find in him also that for which you believe in another God. Come, finally, to the examination of his teachings, disciplines, precepts, and counsels. You will perhaps say that these things are also determined by human laws. But Moses and God were before all Lycurgus and Solon; no posterity does not receive from the beginnings. Nevertheless, my creator did not learn from your God to prescribe: you shall not kill, you shall not commit adultery, you shall not steal, you shall not bear false witness, you shall not covet another's property, honor your father and mother, and love your neighbor as yourself. To these principal counsels of innocence and chastity, justice and piety, are added even precepts of humanity, when with the seventh year also the servitudes are freed by liberty, when at the same time the field is spared, giving place to the needy, when the bonds of the mouth of the ox treading are released for the fruit of the present labor, by which humanity, premeditated in beasts, might be more easily taught in the refreshments of men.

choices.why: using the present participle to describe God's action

pass_b_english: Consider the evidence and you see the whole order of God the Judge laid bare—or, to put it more precisely, the defender of that catholic and supreme goodness which the Marcionites refuse to acknowledge in the same God who sends rain on the good and the evil alike and makes his sun rise on the just and the unjust (Matt. 5:45), a generosity no other god even attempts. Marcion had the audacity to cut this very testimony of Christ about the Creator out of his gospel, but the world itself is written large and every conscience reads it. That same patience of the Creator will stand as evidence against Marcion on judgment day: the patience that waits for a sinner's repentance rather than his death, that prefers mercy to sacrifice. It turned aside the doom decreed for Nineveh, granted Hezekiah an extension on life in answer to his tears, and restored the Babylonian tyrant's kingdom after he repented. This is the mercy that spared Saul's son at the people's pleading, that pardoned David when he confessed his crime against Uriah's house, that restored Israel every time it judged her and recalled her every time it rebuked her. So do not merely stare at the Judge; turn and conform to his supreme example. Mark when he avenges, weigh when he spares; set his gentleness against his severity. When you have taken the measure of both in the Creator, you will find in him the very quality that drove you to invent a second god. Come now, finally, to a close inspection of his teachings, disciplines, precepts, and counsels. You may object that these are merely the stuff of human law codes. But Moses and God preceded every Lycurgus and Solon; no later generation fails to receive from the origins. Still, my Creator did not learn his legislation from your god: 'You shall not kill; you shall not commit adultery; you shall not steal; you shall not bear false witness; you shall not covet your neighbor's goods; honor your father and your mother; and love your neighbor as yourself' (Deut. 5:6–21). To these chief counsels of innocence and chastity, justice and piety, are added precepts of sheer humanity: every seventh year servitudes are dissolved into freedom; at that same time the field is left fallow to give the needy a place; even the ox treading the grain has its muzzle loosened so it may eat of the fruit of its present labor—so that humanity, rehearsed on beasts, might be more easily taught for the relief of human beings.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A provides a faithful literal rendering, and Pass B provides a fluent rendering that correctly identifies the scriptural allusions (Matthew 5:45 and Deuteronomy 5:6-21) which were present in the Latin but not explicitly cited in the source text. The translation of 'boui etiam terenti uincula oris remittuntur' as the ox's muzzle being loosened is accurate. All clauses, including the complex list of God's mercies (Nineveh, Hezekiah, Saul's son, David, Babylon), are preserved.
